correctness.rationale: Every passive species is indexed by a distinct r-tuple, so extinct count at prefix t equals the exact product of removed counts. A pairwise exchange strictly improves any unsaturated imbalanced positive allocation, and decreasing marginal log increments prove optimality of capped level filling. One sequence attains each prefix optimum, proving pointwise dominance. For r=2 the finite arithmetic sum gives exact optimal area and degree-block deficit. The sharp all-graph census uses exact integer DP over all vertex subsets and all graph edge bitmasks through n=5, with no sampling. Re-executed packaged verify.py and checked certificate output. Assumptions explicitly exclude weighted duplicate neighborhoods, rewiring, and post-loss dynamics.

originality.rationale: The inspected original 2015 primary article defines precisely the same extinction-area observable and compares node-degree and nonlinear-ranking heuristics using genetic searches; its results, methods and discussion do not give exact capped balancing, universal prefix dominance, or the five-node obstruction classification. The 2004 primary ecology source motivates extinction sequences but is not an exact placement theorem. Nearby published-finding corpus minimum-sum vertex-cover results optimize first-hit times in the opposite objective direction; they do not logically imply maximizing prefix-induced edges or minimizing last-hit times. Searches by ecological extinction-area names and graph-ordering reductions found no dominating statement. A general earlier ordering theorem could still subsume the structured result; this residual risk is reported and independent novelty certification is not claimed.
residual_risks: The ecological family is highly structured; observations do not directly transfer to realistic heterogeneous networks.
The full text of the 2024 nonlinear-ranking paper and a closely named mathematical ordering problem were not comprehensively excluded; an unknown earlier equivalent exact theorem remains possible.
The finite five-node classification depends on the reproducible exhaustive verifier, not an independent formal or human audit.

value.rationale: Published ecological rankings use extinction area but require approximate search; the theorem solves, for an infinite family with arbitrary guild count and capacities, every removal budget simultaneously rather than only area. It quantifies an exact cubic disadvantage of degree-first targeting in two-community instances and isolates the first possible size and unique isomorphism type of strong degree-ranking failure in all unweighted two-partner systems. These are natural, complete ecological structural results with a direct monitoring/priority-ranking interpretation, not arbitrary slices or isolated code outputs. Limits to structured incidence networks and a specific extinction mechanism are explicit.
